a:r.a:t: Multivalent Adapter Proteins Assemble and Regulate Signalling Cascades

p:cNvPr.descr: Diagram of a scaffold protein from yeast that organizes and regulates a protein kinase cascade. There are two images, a and b. Image (a) shows the scaffold protein, KSR, represented by a long light blue oval, with binding sites at three locations along the right edge. The first site is bound to a darker blue structure labeled Raf, which is bound to a P in a green circle; the second site is bound to another blue structure, MEK, also bound to a P in a green circle; and the third site is bound to a small blue oval, labeled Erk and bound to a P in a green circle as well. A dashed, curved arrow points from Erk to Raf through the long light blue oval. Additionally, there are two small curved arrows – the first one points from Raf to MEK, and the second one points from MEK to Erk. All of the substances that are being phosphorylated (represented by P), have hairline extensions on them to represent activity. At the top of the diagram is a gray arrow pointing downward that reads, “Input.” Below the diagram is a green arrow pointing downward – it reads, “Strong output.” To the right of this drawing is an arrow pointing to the right. Next to it is another KSR protein, but this time it is bound to a P in a red circle, MEK, and Erk. To the right of that at the top is the Raf structure, bound to a P in a green circle, which represents phosphorylation. At the top of this drawing is a gray arrow pointing downward, which reads, “Input.” Below the drawing, a skinny, barely visible green arrow, reads, “Weak output.” In diagram (b), there is a graph of MEK phosphorylation. On the horizontal axis is time, and on the vertical axis is MEK phosphorylation. The graph has two lines; one black and one red. The black like is labeled “Wild type,” and begins at the origin, increases until about a quarter to the right of the horizontal axis and about half way up the vertical axis, and then decreases slightly, forming an imperfect bell curve. The red line, labeled “KSR mutant lacking Erk phosphorylation sites,” begins on a similar trajectory, but increases slightly above the wild type and then plateaus.
